scene: 電車で、降りる駅に着きました。でも、ドアの前に人が立っています。前の人に言います。
question: 何と言いますか。

picture.desc: Inside a train car, the doors are open. Two passengers stand right in front of the open doors with their backs to them. Behind them a young man with a bag on his shoulder leans forward toward the doors and looks at the passenger in front of him.
picture.arrow: the young man behind the two passengers

options: すみません、降ります。
すみません、乗ります。
どうぞ、お先に。

zh.scene: 在电车上，到了要下车的车站。可是门前站着人。对前面的人说。
zh.question: 怎么说？
options: 不好意思，我要下车。
不好意思，我要上车。
您先请。

en.scene: On a train, you've reached your stop, but people are standing in front of the door. You speak to the person in front of you.
en.question: What do you say?
options: Excuse me, I'm getting off.
Excuse me, I'm getting on.
After you.

why.zh: 到站要下车，请前面的人让一下，说「すみません、降ります」。
why.en: You need to get off, so you ask people to let you through: 「すみません、降ります」.

wrong.zh: 「乗ります」是在站台上要上车的人说的，你已经在车上了。
wrong.en: 「乗ります」 is for someone getting on from the platform — you're already aboard.

wrong.zh: 「どうぞ、お先に」是让别人先走，可是要出去的是你自己。
wrong.en: 「どうぞ、お先に」 lets the other person go first — but you're the one who needs to get out.

scene: 友だちが両手に重そうな荷物を持っています。手伝いたいです。友だちに言います。
question: 何と言いますか。

picture.desc: A quiet street. Two young women walk side by side. One carries a big heavy bag in each hand and leans slightly from the weight. The other woman has nothing in her hands and is looking at the bags.

options: 重そうだね。一つ持ってくれる？
重そうだね。一つ持とうか？
重そうだね。一つ持ってきたの？

zh.scene: 朋友两只手都提着看起来很重的东西。你想帮忙。对朋友说。
zh.question: 怎么说？
options: 看起来好重。能帮我拿一个吗？
看起来好重。我帮你拿一个吧？
看起来好重。你带了一个来吗？

en.scene: Your friend has a heavy-looking bag in each hand. You want to help. You speak to your friend.
en.question: What do you say?
options: Looks heavy. Could you carry one for me?
Looks heavy. Shall I take one?
Looks heavy. Did you bring one?

why.zh: 想帮朋友拿东西，用「〜（よ）うか」主动提出：「一つ持とうか」。
why.en: To offer help you use 「〜（よ）うか」: 「一つ持とうか」 — shall I take one?

wrong.zh: 「持ってくれる？」是请朋友帮你拿，立场反了，拿东西的是朋友。
wrong.en: 「持ってくれる？」 asks your friend to carry something for you — backwards; she's the one carrying.

wrong.zh: 「持ってきたの？」是问朋友带没带来，不是提出帮忙。
wrong.en: 「持ってきたの？」 asks whether she brought it — it doesn't offer help.

scene: 店で、棚の高いところにある箱を取りたいですが、手が届きません。近くにいる店の人に言います。
question: 何と言いますか。

picture.desc: A shop aisle with tall plain shelves. A short woman stands on tiptoe, reaching up toward a box on the top shelf that is beyond her fingers. A shop assistant in an apron stands a few steps away, arranging goods on a lower shelf.

options: すみません、あれをお取りしましょうか。
すみません、あれを取ってもいいですか。
すみません、あれを取っていただけませんか。

zh.scene: 在店里，你想拿架子高处的箱子，可是够不着。对旁边的店员说。
zh.question: 怎么说？
options: 不好意思，我帮您拿那个吧？
不好意思，我可以拿那个吗？
不好意思，能帮我拿一下那个吗？

en.scene: In a shop, you want a box from a high shelf but can't reach it. You speak to a shop assistant nearby.
en.question: What do you say?
options: Excuse me, shall I get that for you?
Excuse me, may I take that?
Excuse me, could you get that down for me?

why.zh: 自己够不着，要请店员帮忙拿：「取っていただけませんか」。
why.en: You can't reach it, so you ask the assistant to get it: 「取っていただけませんか」.

wrong.zh: 「お取りしましょうか」是店员主动帮忙时说的，立场反了。
wrong.en: 「お取りしましょうか」 is what the assistant would say offering help — the wrong side.

wrong.zh: 「取ってもいいですか」是问能不能自己拿，可是你够不着，问题没解决。
wrong.en: 「取ってもいいですか」 asks permission to take it yourself — but you can't reach it.

scene: 友だちが、大学の入学試験に合格したと教えてくれました。友だちに言います。
question: 何と言いますか。

picture.desc: A quiet park path. Two young men stand facing each other. One holds a smartphone in one hand and raises the other hand in a happy fist, smiling broadly. The other young man claps his hands and smiles at him.
picture.arrow: the young man who is clapping

options: おかげさまで、合格したよ。
合格おめでとう。よかったね。
あしたの試験、がんばってね。

zh.scene: 朋友告诉你他考上大学了。对朋友说。
zh.question: 怎么说？
options: 托你的福，我考上了。
恭喜你考上了。太好了。
明天的考试加油哦。

en.scene: Your friend has just told you he passed his university entrance exam. You speak to your friend.
en.question: What do you say?
options: Thanks to you, I passed.
Congratulations on passing. That's great.
Good luck in tomorrow's exam.

why.zh: 听到朋友考上了，要祝贺他：「合格おめでとう」。
why.en: Your friend has passed, so you congratulate him: 「合格おめでとう」.

wrong.zh: 「おかげさまで、合格した」是考上的人自己说的，立场反了。
wrong.en: 「おかげさまで、合格した」 is what the person who passed says — the wrong side.

wrong.zh: 考试已经结束、已经考上了，「がんばってね」时机不对。
wrong.en: The exam is over and he has passed — 「がんばってね」 comes too late.
